records.title: Conformal Risk Control
records.authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Stephen Bates, Adam Fisch, Lihua Lei, Tal Schuster
records.mechanism: Extends split conformal prediction to control the expectation of any monotone bounded loss (not just miscoverage) by picking a threshold via a root-finding procedure with a finite-sample guarantee.
records.relevance: Foundational general-purpose risk-control machinery that 'budget under a bound' framings for Story B build on; occupies the generic statistical tool, not the streaming-adaptation-decision application.
records.annotation_source: track sub-agent annotation (mechanism/relevance); bibliographic fields from CrossRef/arXiv/OpenAlex

records.title: Non-Exchangeable Conformal Risk Control
records.authors: António Farinhas, Chrysoula Zerva, Dennis Ulmer, André F. T. Martins
records.mechanism: Extends Conformal Risk Control to non-exchangeable (e.g. sequential/shifted) data using weighted quantiles, retaining a risk bound under distribution drift.
records.relevance: Directly supplies the exchangeability-relaxation needed to apply CRC to a streaming, drifting TSAD setting; a contamination-budget formulation for Story B would need to build on (or distinguish itself from) exactly this relaxation.

records.title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
records.authors: Isaac Gibbs, Emmanuel Candès
records.mechanism: Online update rule (ACI) that adjusts the conformal quantile step-by-step using the realized miscoverage, giving long-run marginal coverage without exchangeability.
records.relevance: Foundational online-conformal adaptation method; any streaming risk-controlled adaptation story must be positioned against ACI and its many follow-ups (below).

records.title: Adaptive Conformal Predictions for Time Series
records.authors: Margaux Zaffran, Aymeric Dieuleveut, Olivier Féron, Yannig Goude, Julie Josse
records.mechanism: Adapts ACI specifically to time series forecasting, analyzing and improving the online quantile-tracking update for sequential, autocorrelated data.
records.relevance: Direct precedent for 'risk-controlled online update for time series'; a TSAD contamination-budget story needs to differentiate from adapting quantiles for forecast intervals to adapting a whole normality model.

records.title: Conformal PID Control for Time Series Prediction
records.authors: Angelopoulos A., Candes E., Tibshirani R.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
records.mechanism: Reframes online conformal quantile-tracking as a feedback-control (PID) problem, adding integral/derivative terms to react to trends and error scale in a time series stream.
records.relevance: Shows the field already treats sequential risk control as a control-theoretic budget-tracking problem for time series; a 'minimize adaptation delay subject to a risk budget' framing needs to explain how it differs from tracking a risk setpoint via PID.

records.authors: Aadyot Bhatnagar, Huan Wang, Caiming Xiong, Yu Bai
records.mechanism: Uses strongly-adaptive online-learning regret bounds to get coverage guarantees that hold over every sub-interval of the stream, not just on long-run average.
records.relevance: Strengthens the online-conformal toolkit with interval-wise (not just asymptotic) guarantees, relevant to bounding transient contamination during a regime change.

records.title: Learn then test: Calibrating predictive algorithms to achieve risk control
records.authors: Angelopoulos A., Bates S., Candès E., Jordan M., Lei L.
records.mechanism: Casts hyperparameter/threshold selection as multiple hypothesis testing, using p-value combination rules to select the largest hyperparameter set with a finite-sample risk guarantee.
records.relevance: General-purpose recipe for turning 'choose an operating threshold so risk <= budget' into a rigorous test; background machinery for any risk-budget story.

records.title: Testing for outliers with conformal p-values
records.authors: Bates S., Candès E., Lei L., Romano Y., Sesia M.
records.mechanism: Constructs conformal p-values for outlier/novelty testing and proves they are positively dependent, enabling exact FDR control with BH-type procedures under exchangeability.

records.title: Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability
records.authors: Barber R., Candès E., Ramdas A., Tibshirani R.
records.mechanism: Generalizes conformal guarantees to non-exchangeable data via weighted conformal scores, quantifying the coverage gap in terms of total-variation distance between the true and assumed exchangeable distributions.
records.relevance: Key theoretical tool for justifying conformal-style guarantees on a genuinely non-stationary TSAD stream; any streaming risk-budget claim needs to be checked against this coverage-gap bound.

records.title: FDR Control for Online Anomaly Detection
records.authors: Etienne Krönert, Alain Célisse, Dalila Hattab
records.mechanism: Online multiple-testing procedure (base 'COAD') that converts anomaly scores into conformal p-values against a calibration set and applies an online FDR control rule so the long-run false-discovery rate of anomaly flags is bounded.
records.relevance: This is the base method the 'online FDR for anomaly alarms' keyword targets; it controls FDR of anomaly *flags*, not of adaptation/model-update decisions — leaves open applying the same guarantee to the update rule itself.

records.title: Breakpoint based online anomaly detection
records.authors: Etienne Krönert, Dalila Hattab, Alain Celisse
records.mechanism: Extends the FDR-controlled online anomaly detector to a setting where the reference (normal) distribution itself evolves, using breakpoint detection to decide when to re-calibrate.
records.relevance: This is the closest existing work to 'FDR-controlled anomaly detection with an evolving normal reference' — i.e., detection with adaptation — but the adaptation trigger is a breakpoint test, not a formal per-step contamination budget on the model update.

records.title: Online Conformal Anomaly Detection with Prediction-Powered Data Acquisition
records.authors: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone
records.mechanism: Wraps any anomaly score in an active/prediction-powered conformal p-value that mixes synthetic (digital-twin) and real calibration data, using the synthetic statistic as a gating signal for when real data is queried, while provably preserving FDR control at every time step.
records.relevance: Shows the 'gate a statistical decision on a cheap proxy, only pay for expensive real evidence when the proxy is uncertain' pattern already exists for anomaly-flag FDR control; a contamination-budget adaptation story would need an analogous gate on the *update*, and must cite this as the template it differs from.

records.title: Tracking the risk of a deployed model and detecting harmful distribution shifts
records.authors: Aleksandr Podkopaev, Aaditya Ramdas
records.mechanism: Uses anytime-valid confidence sequences on a labeled test stream to test H0: running risk of the deployed model stays within tolerance of source risk, raising a time-uniform-controlled alarm exactly when a shift is harmful enough to warrant retraining/intervention.
records.relevance: This is the foundational paper for exactly the 'benign vs. harmful shift, decide whether intervention is warranted, with false-alarm control' framing central to both Story B and Story C — but it needs ground-truth labels and monitors a *static* model, not the adaptation process itself.

records.title: Sequential Harmful Shift Detection Without Labels
records.authors: Amoukou S., Bewley T., Mishra S., Lecue F., Magazzeni D., Veloso M.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
records.mechanism: Extends Podkopaev & Ramdas's sequential harmful-shift test to the label-free setting by substituting a trained error-estimator's proxy loss for the true loss, retaining high detection power and false-alarm control across covariate/label/geographic/temporal shifts.
records.relevance: Direct threat: this is precisely 'sequential, anytime-valid, label-free test to decide harmful-vs-benign shift', the statistical core of Stories B and C, already solved for classification with a proxy-error mechanism. A TSAD adaptation story must show what changes when the object being gated is a *model update* on a non-stationary forecasting/reconstruction task rather than a classifier's error rate.

records.title: Monitoring Risks in Test-Time Adaptation
records.authors: Schirmer M., Jazbec M., Andersson Naesseth C., Nalisnick E.
records.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
records.mechanism: Pairs TTA with a sequential-testing risk monitor extended to (a) a continuously-updated model sequence p1:t instead of a static model and (b) an unsupervised setting using model-uncertainty-based proxy losses; raises a time-uniformly-controlled alarm when the running risk of the *adapting* model exceeds the source risk by a tolerance, signalling the model should be taken offline and retrained.
records.relevance: The single closest published paper to Story C: it explicitly monitors an actively-adapting model (not a frozen one) and outputs a controlled alarm to stop TTA. Gap: binary alarm ('keep adapting' vs 'take offline'), not a three-way ADAPT/FREEZE/UNRESOLVED per-step decision; classification setting with bounded 0-1/Brier loss, not multivariate TSAD; alarm detects 'ultimate failure' after cumulative drift, not a per-update contamination gate.

records.title: WATCH: Adaptive Monitoring for AI Deployments via Weighted-Conformal Martingales
records.authors: Drew Prinster, Xing Han, Anqi Liu, Suchi Saria
records.mechanism: Generalizes conformal test martingales to weighted/non-exchangeable settings for continual post-deployment monitoring of arbitrary hypotheses about model behaviour, giving anytime-valid alarms.
records.relevance: Another anytime-valid monitoring framework for deployed-model risk; reinforces that conformal-martingale gating of model-behaviour hypotheses is an active, multi-group line (cf. arXiv:2608.30502 already inventoried) that any new gating mechanism must be benchmarked against.

records.authors: Ramdas A., Grünwald P., Vovk V., Shafer G.
records.mechanism: Survey/unification of e-processes, test martingales, and confidence sequences as the common machinery for anytime-valid (safe under optional stopping/continuation) statistical inference.

records.authors: Shin J., Ramdas A., Rinaldo A.
records.venue: The New England Journal of Statistics in Data Science
